summary: Port reproduces the original's fire simulation faithfully in structure, all four flame modes, motion speed and every control, but its palette whitens far too much at the hot end, its flame texture is spatially smoothed (few isolated sparks), it burns ~15% shorter, and its sliderMode is quantized into four equal quarters where the original uses round(mode*3).
observations: Both sides render alive with no compile or runtime errors on the default rig (strip, 60 px, seed 1). Baseline 6 s / 20 fps: orig meanBrightness avg 27.3 motion avg 8.2; port 26.4 / 7.1. zeroMotionFrames = 1 on both (the mandatory first-frame zero).

Control surface is IDENTICAL on both sides — same five controls, same names, same kinds: hsvPickerColor (hsvPicker, 'Color'), sliderFlameHeight, sliderHeat, sliderSparks, sliderMode (all slider). No missing or invented dials.

No time regimes on either side: a 60 s / 5 fps survey and a 240 s / 2 fps extended survey both show a uniform stochastic fire texture start to finish. Steady-state check (--skip 120, 30 s @ 4 fps) gives brightnessTrend 'steady' on BOTH sides, zeroMotionFrames 0, orig mean 28.5 / port 27.4. The port does not die, freeze or drift.

MOTION MATCHES at the default rate. Residual-field cross-correlation over 100 consecutive dumped frames (skip 10, 20 fps) puts the peak at shift +2 px for lag 1 frame on BOTH sides (orig corr 0.96, port 0.65) and shift +4 px for lag 2 (orig 0.93, port 0.50): both advect toward the flame tip at 2 px/frame = 40 px/s.

FRAME-RATE COUPLING DIFFERS BELOW 20 fps. At --fps 10 the orig still advances only 2 px/frame (20 px/s) while the port advances 4 px/frame (40 px/s); at --fps 40 both advance 1 px/frame (40 px/s, orig lag-2 corr 0.97). So the original's advection is capped at one ~2 px step per rendered frame (a 20 Hz tick that does not catch up), while the port integrates elapsed time linearly. The two agree exactly at >= 20 fps, so this only bites at low frame rates.

TEXTURE CHARACTER DIVERGES. Time-averaged spatial roughness (mean |neighbour difference| of pixel brightness over 80 frames): orig 8.8, port 6.5. Detrended neighbour correlation of the per-pixel residual: orig 0.01 (even pairs) / 0.05 (odd pairs) — every pixel flickers independently; port 0.63 / 0.53 — the port's flicker is a spatially smooth/correlated noise field. Visually the orig waterfall is a grainy dotted diagonal texture, the port's is continuous smooth streaks.

TEMPORAL COHERENCE DIVERGES the other way: residual autocorrelation at lag 1 frame (20 fps, motion-compensated) is 0.96 on the orig vs 0.65 on the port — the port re-randomizes its flame texture noticeably faster from frame to frame.

The original's TIME-AVERAGED brightness profile has a clear 2-pixel staircase (px0..: 135.3 132.8 | 114.0 110.2 | 95.4 94.6 | 77.6 78.2 | 67.6 69.3 | 58.8 60.3 | 51.6 52.6 | 44.3 44.6 | 35.7 35.7 | 31.2 31.3 ...), i.e. its heat field is at half the strip resolution (~30 cells over 60 px) with independent per-pixel flicker on top. The port's profile is smooth per pixel with no pairing (160 152 132 117 111 94 85 73 65 61 56 52 47 43 ...).

FLAME REACH / BASE HEAT. Untouched defaults, mean over 80 frames spanning 5-25 s: orig base pixel 135, port 160 (port ~18% hotter at the base); orig profile falls below 2 at px ~46 and to 0 at px ~51, port falls below 2 at px ~41 and to 0 at px ~42 — the port's flame is roughly 15-20% shorter. Same relation at sliderHeat=1 (orig reach 45, port 35).

PALETTE DIVERGENCE (the most visible difference). Binning untouched output by max channel, mean RGB per bin — orig vs port: 0-31 (18,0,0) vs (17,3,0); 32-63 (46,5,0) vs (46,11,0); 64-95 (79,14,0) vs (79,21,0); 96-127 (111,29,0) vs (112,35,0); 128-159 (143,48,0) vs (142,55,8); 160-191 (175,72,0) vs (175,88,33); 192-223 (208,109,14) vs (207,126,65); 224-255 (238,153,44) vs (238,166,104). Red channel matches exactly; green runs +6..+17 high on the port and blue runs far higher (44 -> 104 at the top bin).

Same fact as saturation: mean HSV saturation by value decile, untouched — orig stays 1.00 up to v=0.7 and only drops to 0.91 / 0.81 in the top two deciles; port starts desaturating at v=0.5 and reads 0.85 / 0.75 / 0.65 / 0.55 in the top four. Over bright pixels (R>150) B/R is 0.060 on the orig and 0.275 on the port, G/R 0.491 vs 0.571. The port's flame tips look pale peach where the original's are deep amber.
Whole-window colour means confirm it: baseline meanB avg 2.1 (orig) vs 7.7 (port); meanR 59.1 vs 49.8.

SPARK DENSITY. Fraction of mid-strip pixels (index 6-49) exceeding 2.2x their 8-neighbour mean, 60 frames over 22 s: orig 0.0152 / 0.0197 / 0.0155 / 0.0246 / 0.0284 at sliderSparks 0 / 0.25 / 0.5 / 0.75 / 1; port 0.0083 / 0.0057 / 0.0064 / 0.0068 / 0.0114. The port has ~2-3x fewer isolated sparks at every setting (consequence of its smoothed noise field).

ALL FOUR MODES EXIST ON BOTH SIDES and look structurally the same: M0 = fire from the left end; M1 = fire from the right end; M2 = fire from the centre outward (bright centre, dark ends); M3 = fire from both ends inward (bright ends, dark centre). Confirmed by per-region brightness dumps and by the mode-1 / mode-0.55 / ms-0.30 waterfalls, which mirror each other correctly.

MODE BOUNDARY MAPPING DIFFERS. Bisected boundaries: orig switches at 0.1665 (0.16 -> M0, 0.17 -> M1), at 0.50 (0.50 -> M2), and at ~0.8335 (0.833 -> M2, 0.84 -> M3) — i.e. round(mode*3), so M0 and M3 occupy half-width bands. Port switches at ~0.25 (0.25 -> M0, 0.26 -> M1), ~0.505 (0.50 -> M1, 0.51 -> M2) and ~0.755 (0.75 -> M2, 0.76 -> M3) — four equal quarters. Result: for sliderMode in [0.167, 0.25) the orig draws right-fire while the port draws left-fire, and for (0.75, 0.833] the orig draws centre-out while the port draws edges-in. About 1/6 of the slider's range selects a different mode.
Seed independence: seeds 7 and 1234 give the same summary statistics as seed 1 on both sides (orig mean 27-28 motion 8-9; port mean 26 motion 7), so nothing here is a one-seed fluke.

dials.name: hsvPickerColor
dials.origEffect: Sets the flame hue. Sweeping h at s=1,v=1 over 0 / 0.15 / 0.33 / 0.5 / 0.66 / 0.85 gives circular-mean hue of the lit pixels 0.073 / 0.216 / 0.403 / 0.567 / 0.734 / 0.919 — tracks the picker with a constant ~+0.07 offset; mean saturation 0.99 with only the top value decile whitening to 0.94.
dials.portEffect: Same behaviour and same direction: 0.040 / 0.182 / 0.370 / 0.533 / 0.700 / 0.883 — tracks the picker with a ~+0.035 offset, i.e. about 12 degrees less hue offset than the original. Mean saturation 0.96, top decile 0.84 (still whiter than the orig).

dials.name: sliderFlameHeight
dials.origEffect: Sets how far the flame climbs. At 0 only the base burns (mean profile >= 2 out to px 8, base 69); at 0.5 out to px 12 (base 96, px10 = 2); at 1 the whole 60-px strip burns (base 154, px10 103, px20 72, px30 58, reach 59).
dials.portEffect: Same direction and roughly the same scale: 0 -> reach 6 (base 91); 0.5 -> reach 13 (base 122, px10 11); 1 -> reach 59 (base 179, px10 133, px20 73, px30 69). Port runs consistently hotter at the base and fills the mid-strip slightly more at 0.5.

dials.name: sliderHeat
dials.origEffect: Overall fire intensity. 0 -> essentially dark (base 4, reach 4, no bright pixels); 0.5 -> base 30, px10 12, reach 24; 1 -> base 139, px10 58, px20 23, reach 45.
dials.portEffect: Same direction and near-identical base values: 0 -> base 5 (reach 12, i.e. a dimmer but longer ember tail than the orig); 0.5 -> base 32, px10 13, reach 19; 1 -> base 160, px10 62, px20 13, reach 35. Port's flame is consistently shorter at high heat (35 vs 45).

dials.name: sliderSparks
dials.origEffect: Raises the density of isolated bright single-pixel sparks in the flame body. Measured spark rate over 60 frames / 22 s: 0.0152 at 0 rising to 0.0284 at 1 (~1.9x). Peak pixel brightness in the mid-strip also rises (95 at 0, 165 at 1).
dials.portEffect: Same direction but much weaker and from a much lower floor: 0.0083 at 0 rising to 0.0114 at 1 (~1.4x), i.e. 2-3x fewer sparks than the original at every setting. Peak mid-strip brightness rises comparably (123 at 0, 164 at 1).

dials.name: sliderMode
dials.origEffect: Selects one of four flame geometries — left-fire / right-fire / centre-out / edges-in. Boundaries bisected at 0.1665, 0.500 and 0.8335 (round(mode*3)), so the first and last modes each occupy only half-width bands of the slider.
dials.portEffect: Selects the same four geometries, drawn the same way, but boundaries sit at ~0.25, ~0.505 and ~0.755 — four equal quarters. sliderMode in [0.167, 0.25) and (0.75, 0.833] therefore select a different mode on the two sides.

feedback: PALETTE: the port whitens far too aggressively at the hot end. At matched red level the original's ramp is (175,72,0) / (208,109,14) / (238,153,44) where the port renders (175,88,33) / (207,126,65) / (238,166,104). Green needs to come down roughly 10-15 units through the upper half of the ramp and blue needs to stay near 0 until red is above ~190 and then rise only to ~45 at full — the original stays fully saturated (HSV S = 1.00) until value ~0.7 and bottoms out at S ~ 0.81, while the port is already at S 0.85 by value 0.6 and reaches S 0.55. Aim for deep amber tips, not peach.

TEXTURE: the port's flicker is a spatially smooth noise field (detrended neighbour correlation 0.53-0.63) where the original's is independent per pixel (0.01-0.05). The original also carries a half-resolution heat base — its time-averaged profile shows 2-pixel plateaus (95.4/94.6, 77.6/78.2, 35.7/35.7) — with the per-pixel randomness layered on top. Reproducing that combination (heat computed on ~30 cells for a 60 px strip, then a per-pixel independent flicker/spark multiplier) would fix both the graininess and the spark-density gap in one move.

SPARKS: at every sliderSparks setting the port produces 2-3x fewer isolated bright pixels than the original (0.008-0.011 vs 0.015-0.028 of mid-strip pixels above 2.2x their local neighbourhood), and its response to the dial is shallower (1.4x from 0 to 1 vs 1.9x). Raise the base spark rate to about 1.5% of mid-strip pixels at sliderSparks=0 and about 2.8% at 1.

MODE MAPPING: the port bins sliderMode into four equal quarters (boundaries 0.25 / 0.50 / 0.75). The original uses round(mode*3): boundaries at 1/6, 1/2 and 5/6, so modes 0 and 3 occupy only half-width bands. Change the quantization so sliderMode 0.20 lands on right-fire (currently left-fire on the port) and 0.80 lands on centre-out (currently edges-in).

FLAME GEOMETRY: at the untouched defaults the port's base is ~18% hotter (mean base pixel 160 vs 135) while its flame dies out ~15-20% sooner (mean profile hits 0 at px ~42 vs ~51; at sliderHeat=1, reach 35 vs 45). Reduce the base heat slightly and lengthen the decay so the tail reaches into the high 40s of a 60 px strip at default settings.

FRAME-RATE COUPLING (minor): the original advances the flame at most one ~2 px step per rendered frame (measured 2 px/frame at both 10 and 20 fps, 1 px/frame at 40 fps), whereas the port advances linearly with elapsed time (4 / 2 / 1 px/frame at 10 / 20 / 40 fps). They agree at 20 fps and above; only sub-20 fps rendering diverges, so this is worth matching only if low-frame-rate fidelity matters.
COLOR DIAL (nitpick): the original's hue lands about +0.07 above the picker hue, the port's about +0.035 — a constant ~12 degree hue offset difference across the whole sweep.
